name: Antiochus Epiphanes
charge: Defiling the temple; forbidding the law; murdering the faithful
summary: The Seleucid king outlawed the law of Moses, defiled the temple with an idol, and put to death those who kept the covenant. The books of Maccabees record both his persecution and his end.
offense: He forbade circumcision and the sabbaths, set up the abomination on the altar, forced sacrifice to idols, and killed mothers who circumcised their sons and families who kept the law in secret.
judgment: Struck with an incurable disease of the bowels, worms rising from the living body, he died in a strange land in bitter grief, by the account, confessing at the last that it was right to be subject to God.

entries.commentary: In the first year of Darius the Mede, the messenger stood to confirm and to strengthen him.

Three more kings would stand up in Persia: Cyrus, Cambyses, and Darius. The fourth would be far richer than they all. This is Xerxes, who profited from all that the kingdom had already gained, and by his strength through his riches he stirred up all against the realm of Grecia. This is where they gathered all the heathen together and formed the Greeks. They conquered the original Greeks and named themselves the Greeks, and all the nations, even some of my own tribes, came together and were called the Greeks.

The mighty king that stands up and rules with great dominion, doing according to his will, is Alexander the Greek. When a nation is a superpower it does what it will and nobody can stop it, the same as America does today. When he stood up his kingdom was broken, because he eventually died and left no children, so it was not passed to his posterity. His kingdom was divided toward the four winds of heaven, to his four generals, Cassander, Lysimachus, Seleucus, and Ptolemy, not according to his own dominion.
The king of the south that grows strong is Ptolemy, who was over Egypt. One of his princes grows strong above him with a great dominion. Out of Ptolemy came Antiochus.

In the end of years they join themselves together, and the king's daughter of the south comes to the king of the north to make an agreement. She does not retain the power of the arm, neither does he stand nor his arm. The power of the arm is Antiochus' strength.

Out of a branch of her roots one stands up in her estate, comes with an army, enters the fortress of the king of the north, deals against them and prevails. It was actual war over the kingdoms. He carries captives into Egypt, their gods with their princes and their precious vessels of silver and gold, for Ptolemy was over Egypt, and he continues more years than the king of the north.

His sons are stirred up, assemble a multitude of great forces, and one comes and overflows and passes through, even to his fortress. The king of the south is moved with anger, comes forth, and fights the king of the north, who sets forth a great multitude, but the multitude is given into the hand of the south. When he has taken away the multitude his heart is lifted up and he becomes prideful, casting down many ten thousands, but he is not strengthened by it.
The king of the north returns and sets forth a multitude greater than the former, coming after certain years with a great army and much riches.

In those times many stand up against the king of the south, meaning Ptolemy. The robbers of thy people, the heathen, the Greeks who robbed Israel, exalt themselves to establish the vision, but they shall fall.

The king of the north comes up, casts up a mount, and takes the most fenced cities, and the arms of the south cannot withstand, neither his chosen people, meaning Israel, nor any strength to withstand. He that comes against him does according to his own will, and none stands before him, because he is the power at this time, and he stands in the glorious land which is consumed by his hand.

He sets his face to enter with the strength of his whole kingdom, and gives him the daughter of women, corrupting her, but she does not stand on his side. He turns his face unto the isles of the coastline and takes many, but a prince causes the reproach he offered to cease and turns it back upon him. Someone causes him to stop conquering land, so he is conquered and falls, and this goes to Ptolemy. Then he turns his face toward the fort of his own land, but he stumbles and falls and is not found.
In his estate stands up a raiser of taxes in the glory of the kingdom, a ruler taxing and ruling the people, but within few days he is destroyed, neither in anger nor in battle.
In his estate stands up a vile person to whom they do not give the honor of the kingdom, but he comes in peaceably and obtains the kingdom by flatteries. -
With the arms of a flood they are overflown and broken from before him, yea also the prince of the covenant, and after the league made with him he works deceitfully. -

After the league is made he works deceitfully, this being Jason working deceitfully against his own people. He comes up and becomes strong with a small people. He enters peaceably even upon the fattest places of the province, the best places of the land, and does what his fathers and his fathers' fathers had not done, scattering among them the prey and spoil and riches, going against his own people for riches.
He stirs up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south is stirred up to battle with a very great and mighty army. -

They that feed of the portion of his meat destroy him, his army overflows, and many fall down slain. Both these kings' hearts are set to do mischief, and they speak lies at one table, but it does not prosper, for the end is yet at the time appointed.
Then he returns into his land with great riches, and his heart is against the holy covenant. -

At the time appointed he returns toward the south, but it is not as the former, for the ships of Chittim come against him, therefore he is grieved and has indignation against the holy covenant. He returns and has intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant, because our people were forsaking the laws at this time. -
An arm stands on his part, they pollute the sanctuary of strength, take away the daily sacrifice, and place the abomination that maketh desolate. -

Such as do wickedly against the covenant he corrupts by flatteries, but the people that do know their God shall be strong and do exploits. They that understand among the people instruct many, yet they fall by the sword, by flame, by captivity, and by spoil many days, and some of understanding fall to try them, to purge, and to make them white, even to the time of the end. -

The king does according to his will, exalts and magnifies himself above every god, and speaks marvelous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the indignation is accomplished. He does not regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor any god, for he magnifies himself above all. In his estate he honors the god of forces, a god whom his fathers knew not, with gold and silver and precious stones, and he causes them to rule over many and divides the land for gain.

At the time of the end the king of the south pushes at him, and the king of the north comes against him like a whirlwind with chariots and horsemen and many ships, and enters into the countries and overflows and passes over. He enters the glorious land, and many countries are overthrown, but Edom and Moab and the chief of the children of Ammon escape out of his hand. He stretches his hand upon the countries, and Egypt does not escape, and he has power over the treasures of gold and silver, with the Libyans and the Ethiopians at his steps. Tidings out of the east and north trouble him, so he goes forth with great fury to destroy, and plants the tabernacles of his palace between the seas in the glorious holy mountain, yet he comes to his end and none shall help him.

verses.text: Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people,
And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king.
Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.
For the king had sent letters by messengers unto Jerusalem and the cities of Juda that they should follow the strange laws of the land,
And forbid burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and drink offerings, in the temple; and that they should profane the sabbaths and festival days:
And pollute the sanctuary and holy people:
Set up altars, and groves, and chapels of idols, and sacrifice swine’s flesh, and unclean beasts:
That they should also leave their children uncircumcised, and make their souls abominable with all manner of uncleanness and profanation:
To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.
And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.

Now the fifteenth day of the month Casleu, in the hundred forty and fifth year, they set up the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and builded idol altars throughout the cities of Juda on every side;
And burnt incense at the doors of their houses, and in the streets.
And when they had rent in pieces the books of the law which they found, they burnt them with fire.
And whosoever was found with any the book of the testament, or if any committed to the law, the king’s commandment was, that they should put him to death.
Thus did they by their authority unto the Israelites every month, to as many as were found in the cities.
Now the five and twentieth day of the month they did sacrifice upon the idol altar, which was upon the altar of God.
At which time according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised.
And they hanged the infants about their necks, and rifled their houses, and slew them that had circumcised them.
Howbeit many in Israel were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat any unclean thing.
Wherefore the rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.
And there was very great wrath upon Israel.
Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God:
And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place.

But the Lord Almighty, the God of Isreal, smote him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;
And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.

Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews, and commanding to haste the journey: but it came to pass that he fell down from his chariot, carried violently; so that having a sore fall, all the members of his body were much pained.

And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground, and carried in an horselitter, shewing forth unto all the manifest power of God.
So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.
And the man, that thought a little afore he could reach to the stars of heaven, no man could endure to carry for his intolerable stink.
And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.
Now when the king heard these words, he was astonished and sore moved: whereupon he laid him down upon his bed, and fell sick for grief, because it had not befallen him as he looked for.
And there he continued many days: for his grief was ever more and more, and he made account that he should die.
Wherefore he called for all his friends, and said unto them, The sleep is gone from mine eyes, and my heart faileth for very care.
And I thought with myself, Into what tribulation am I come, and how great a flood of misery is it, wherein now I am! for I was bountiful and beloved in my power.
But now I remember the evils that I did at Jerusalem, and that I took all the vessels of gold and silver that were therein, and sent to destroy the inhabitants of Judea without a cause.
I perceive therefore that for this cause these troubles are come upon me, and, behold, I perish through great grief in a strange land.

lawsResolved.text: I am the LORD your God, you shall have no other gods besides me.
Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
